claims.text: In situ aberration-corrected high-resolution TEM with a high-temperature holder can directly observe atomic-scale structural transformations in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Observed structural transformations would validate thermodynamically driven phase changes that underpin enhanced thermal stability.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a uniform, single-phase atomic distribution at room temperature.
The nanoparticles will be heated in situ while undergoing aberration-corrected high-resolution TEM imaging.
Temperature will be increased gradually from room temperature under a controlled vacuum or inert-gas environment.
Heating may produce local lattice distortions, phase separation, or ordering in the nanoparticles.
Thermal energy overcomes kinetic barriers and induces atomic rearrangements.
Thermally induced atomic rearrangements lead to observable phase transformations.
Aberration-corrected TEM can capture the proposed transformations in real time.
Elevated temperature will transform the homogeneous solid solution into phase-separated or ordered structures.
Phase separation or ordering will be evidenced by changed lattice spacings or the emergence of distinct phase boundaries.
Room-temperature imaging will show a uniform atomic distribution without phase separation or ordering.
The observations are limited by TEM resolution and the accessible temperature range.
Composition deviations and nanoparticle-size effects may alter the thermal behavior.
The onset temperature and magnitude of atomic rearrangements are uncertain because of nanoparticle-size effects and experimental variability.
